source.title: GPT-2 Through the Lens of Vector Symbolic Architectures
source.authors: Johannes Knittel; Tushaar Gangavarapu; Hendrik Strobelt; Hanspeter Pfister

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: It analyzes GPT-2 using weight geometry and neuron-to-vector similarity rather than testing the original toy-network setup, and reports results bearing on indirect evidence for feature-like directions in a language model.
record.gate_note: The paper tests GPT-2 for VSA-like near-orthogonal vectors and bundled neuron weights. It does not test toy networks, feature sparsity or importance sweeps, capacity competition, or SAE recovery. The reported cosine similarities and geometric observations are results; the paper's theoretical descriptions of attention and MLP operations are not treated as results.
record.test_reason: It reports weight-geometry results on pretrained GPT-2 small. The word-embedding and MLP-output M⊺M analyses show many more nearly orthogonal directions than residual dimensions, which is indirect evidence for V4 in a real LM. The rest of the paper mostly tests the authors' VSA bundling/binding framework rather than any listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that GPT-2 small appears to use VSA-like bundling and binding of nearly orthogonal vectors, and that some neurons implement simple boolean functions. They say this strengthens the validity of training SAEs, but the vectors may not be interpretable or independent features and may be part of multidimensional features. They call the findings preliminary and limited to GPT-2 small.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes a pretrained GPT-2 model's weights and vectors using matrix geometry and greedy cosine-similarity matches; it does not use the original toy-model setup or its feature-sparsity experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors chose similarity thresholds for the greedy bundling method, but report no outcome comparison across threshold settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Greedy unweighted sums of token embeddings and attention/MLP output vectors reach cosine ≥0.3 with input weights for >95% of layer-0 neurons and 30–50% of middle-layer neurons. Example neurons reach 0.69–0.91.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MLP neuron input weights in GPT-2 are approximately bundles (OR-sums) of nearly orthogonal upstream vectors.

fits_no_version.finding: Zeroing neuron 7-1321 lowers the 'to' logit for 'In relation' but not for 'I was listening'.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A neuron's intervention effect on a token logit is prompt-specific.

record.peer_reviewed: 2nd Workshop on Attributing Model Behavior at Scale (ATTRIB) at NeurIPS 2024
record.problems: The study examines only GPT-2 small. Its neuron-to-vector explanations use a greedy similarity method and the authors note that the method assumes some monosemanticity in individual neurons and attention dimensions. The analysis is based on weights rather than activation observations, and no SAE-based analysis is performed.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweeps, phase transitions or geometry analysis.
No test of capacity competition or of feature importance.
No test of non-capacity causes of polysemanticity.
No SAE recovery, and no activation-level test of features spread across neurons; only weight geometry.
No SAE features are trained or evaluated.
Not tested. The authors only speculate that the vectors may be part of multidimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: Workshop paper. No controls or random baselines for either the orthogonality plots or the greedy bundling similarities. The greedy method could plausibly reach moderate cosine against arbitrary vectors given 50k candidate embeddings. The V4 support is therefore weak, and most quantitative results concern the authors' VSA framework rather than superposition versions.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks or sparsity-dependent transitions or regular geometries are tested.
No test of capacity pressure, feature importance, or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
No test of alternative causes of polysemanticity or whether polysemanticity alone indicates superposition.
The study examines GPT-2 small weights and vector geometry, but does not test feature spread using activation-level feature attribution or SAE recovery.
No SAE features are trained or assessed for completeness, stability, or canonical status.
The study does not empirically distinguish one-dimensional features from multidimensional features.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Computed M⊺M for word embeddings and assessed its geometry.
rows.measure: Near-orthogonality of vectors, assessed from the matrix product.
rows.value: Strong diagonals with minimal artifacts; the paper says this suggests the vectors are nearly orthogonal.
rows.note: The paper gives this as a qualitative result and refers to visualizations in Appendix B.
rows.check: Qualitative only, with no random-vector baseline. 50k embeddings in 768 dims being nearly orthogonal is consistent with superposition, but random high-dimensional vectors would also show this.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Computed M⊺M for attention matrices and assessed its geometry.
rows.measure: Near-orthogonality of vectors, assessed from the matrix product.
rows.value: Strong diagonals with minimal artifacts; the paper says this suggests the matrices are composed of nearly orthogonal vectors.
rows.note: The paper says the result holds in all cases it examined; the figure shows an exemplary selection.
rows.check: Per-head attention matrices have no more vectors than dimensions. Near-orthogonality here bears on the authors' binding interpretation, not on features overlapping beyond capacity.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Computed M⊺M for MLP output projections and assessed its geometry.
rows.measure: Near-orthogonality of vectors, assessed from the matrix product.
rows.value: Strong diagonals with minimal artifacts; the paper says this suggests the matrices are composed of nearly orthogonal vectors.
rows.note: The figure shows exemplary visualizations, not an exhaustive set.
rows.check: Qualitative; Figure 4 shows only a top-left excerpt of 3072 vectors in 768 dims, with no random baseline.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Compared first-layer MLP input weights with greedily assembled unweighted sums of word embeddings.
rows.measure: Share of neurons whose weights were explained by a bundled vector at the stated cosine threshold.
rows.note: The authors say this includes attributions to attention heads discussed in the following section.
rows.check: Measures how well greedy unweighted sums of embeddings match neuron input weights, with no random or null baseline. This is not a measure of features spread across neurons or of SAE-recoverable features.

relationships.condition: GPT-2 small, word embeddings and MLP output projections (weights only, qualitative M⊺M plots)
relationships.reason: Many more vectors than dimensions are reported as nearly orthogonal (r1, r3). This is weak indirect support: there is no random baseline and no numbers.
relationships.display_finding: Many more vectors than dimensions appeared nearly orthogonal in the M⊺M plots. The support is weak, with no random baseline and no numbers.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
